english.title: Attempt to bring / throw / convey List ' A ' prohibited article into / out of a prison on behalf of a prisoner
english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..), without authorisation, attempted to bring, throw or otherwise convey

(A)_[an article, namely **(..SPECIFY THE ARTICLE..),]_
(B)_[a substance, namely **(..SPECIFY THE SUBSTANCE..),]_

which had been prescribed for the purposes of section 40A(2) of the Prison Act 1952 by prison rules, into or out of

(C)_[His Majesty's prison situated at **(..SPECIFY THE LOCATION..)]_
(D)_[His Majesty's remand centre situated at **(..SPECIFY THE LOCATION..), being an institution to which section 43 of the Prison Act 1952 applied,]_
(E)_[His Majesty's young offender institution situated at **(..SPECIFY THE LOCATION..), being an institution to which section 43 of the Prison Act 1952 applied,]_
(F)_[His Majesty's secure training centre situated at **(..SPECIFY THE LOCATION..), being an institution to which section 43 of the Prison Act 1952 applied,]_

on behalf of a prisoner

english.notes:
(i) This offence was substituted for section 40 of the Prison Act 1952 by section 22 of the Offender Management Act 2007 with effect from 01/04/08.
(ii) Section 40A(2) of the Prison Act 1952 provides that such a List ' A ' prohibited article includes
(a) a controlled drug (as defined for the purposes of the Misuse of Drugs Act 1971);
(b) an explosive;
(c) any firearm or ammunition (as defined in section 57 of the Firearms Act 1968);
(d) any other offensive weapon (as defined in section 1(9) of the Police and Criminal Evidence Act 1984).
(iii) See subsections 40B(2), (3), (4) and (5) of the Prison Act 1952 as inserted by section 22 of the Offender Management Act 2007 for the meaning of and who may issue an "authorisation".
(iv) Section 40C(4) of the Prison Act 1952 provides that in proceedings for an offence under this section it is a defence for the accused to show that:-
(a) he reasonably believed that he had authorisation to do the act in respect of which the proceedings are brought, or
(b) in all the circumstances there was an overriding public interest which justified the doing of that act.
(v) Section 10 of the Interpretation Act 1978 states that any reference to the Sovereign reigning at the time of the passing of the Act is to be construed, unless the contrary intention appears, as a reference to the Sovereign for the time being. As such, references to ‘Her Majesty’ and ‘the Queen’ have been replaced in the wording of the offences to state ‘His Majesty’ or ‘the King’, although this may not be the strict wording of the legislation.
